articles.title: Mass. teen charged with killing mother, brother after using ChatGPT to explore ‘fantasy stories’ of family’s deaths
articles.summary: The suspect used the “internet and ChatGPT to make searches for theoretical ideas or fantasy stories regarding the killing of his family,” the DA said.
articles.body: A Massachusetts teenager used a laptop and a knife to beat his mother and brother to death, hours after he used ChatGPT to search “for theoretical ideas or fantasy stories regarding the killing of his family,” prosecutors said Thursday. Arjun Aravind, 17, of the affluent Boston suburb of Acton, was charged with two counts of murder in the deaths of Sudha Venkatesan, 45, and Siddharth Aravind, 14, according to a criminal complaint filed in Concord. He also faces assault and battery charges, accused of using “a dangerous weapon, a Laptop,” to attack his two victims, the complaint says. Investigators said that “a heavily damaged bloody laptop computer was found consistent with it being used during the assault,” according to the complaint. Police also recovered what appeared to be a knife that was used in the attack: “A bent utensil, possibly a knife with an orange handle, was also found in the area of the disturbance,” the complaint said. Aravind had been having “behavioral issues” with “concerning internet activities” — to the point that “the family was hiding knives in the household” to prevent his “having access to them,” according to the complaint. Acton police officers arrived at the family home on Martha Lane at 6:37 p.m. Tuesday to conduct a welfare check. Aravind’s tutor, who had a 4 p.m. appointment at the home that day, “was unable to make contact with residents upon arrival,” prosecutors said. Shortly afterward, Aravind’s father — who had left for work hours earlier — called police. Officers “found both victims dead inside,” the district attorney said. Siddharth’s body was found on the first floor; Venkatesan’s was found in the basement. The younger victim was found “with massive trauma to the head” and “lying in a pool of blood,” the complaint said. Venkatesan was found with “heavy trauma” to her head and face, along with “a puncture rod to her stomach consistent with some object being used as a weapon,” according to the document. “As officers cleared the residence, significant biological evidence was observed in and around the bodies,” the probable cause statement said. Hours before the killings, Aravind had typed into ChatGPT, “wait when Adrian kills parents I could see him luring one to convo in basement as they have always forced him to do but what excuse would he use to take their phone” and “maybe before killing mom Adrian coldly reveals,” according to the complaint. “The investigation has so far shown that Arjun had recently been demonstrating some concerning behavior, including using the internet and ChatGPT to make searches for theoretical ideas or fantasy stories regarding the killing of his family,” Middlesex County DA Marian Ryan told reporters Wednesday. A representative for OpenAI, the San Francisco-based developer of ChatGPT, could not immediately be reached for comment Thursday. “He was engaged in the use of ChatGPT in creating fantasy stories, kind of the gothic novel kind of stories, asking questions, creating characters, asking what about this if this happened to that, and they seem to appear to relate to threats to his family,” Ryan added. It’s unclear which victim was killed first. The suspect’s brother had gone to a recreational facility around 9 a.m. and returned home shortly after noon, Ryan said. “This is an unspeakable tragedy,” Ryan said. “It is an incredibly dark day. Obviously, an insurmountable tragedy for the dad in this case.” Aravind and his mother’s car — a 2014 green Honda Accord — were missing from the home when the bodies were discovered. An alarm was tripped at a parking lot about 13 miles away in Wayland early Wednesday. Officers “recognized that license plate, and Arjun was inside that car,” Ryan said. “He was taken into custody by police without incident,” she added. Aravind was found asleep in the vehicle; officers found bedding and “large amounts of cereal and protein energy bars,” according to the complaint. A person, whose name was redacted from the court document, had been to a nearby supermarket at about 4 p.m. Tuesday and purchased “an enormous” amount of cereal and energy bars. “This employee reported this purchased was in excess of $2,000 and when questioned, he reported he had plans to sell the items,” according to the complaint. Local law enforcement had previous contact with the family after Aravind was reported missing the previous year. Acton Police Chief Douglas Sturniolo said that incident was treated as a runaway case and involved no threats of violence. Defense lawyer Debra DeWit urged the public to reserve judgment. “My client is distraught and confused,” she told NBC News on Thursday. “It’s a tragedy for everyone.” Aravind pleaded not guilty Thursday and was ordered held without bail.

articles.title: Big Ten, SEC approve ban on pro players returning to college to play; ACC, Big 12 considering move
articles.summary: The SEC announced Monday night that professionals should not "return to college competition."
articles.body:
With the Big Ten making the first move, the ACC and Big 12 are now also considering a ban on former professional players who want to return to play in college, according to Yahoo Sports' Ross Dellenger .

The Big Ten formally adopted that policy on Tuesday, officially making underclassmen who declared for the NFL Draft and didn't withdraw, signed pro contracts or appeared on an NFL roster ineligible. The Big Ten's vote was unanimous.

"The conference continues to evaluate potential rules restricting professional athletes in other sports from conference competition," the league said in a statement, in part.

The Big Ten later announced the penalties for violating the rule: a coach suspension of 50% of the season and an institutional fine .

Then on Tuesday afternoon, the SEC followed suit. The conference announced a similar policy for both football and basketball. The Big Ten's move only included football.

Notre Dame officials have told the Big Ten and SEC that it the school will also follow a similar policy.

The flurry of discussions comes after the reports that Dae'Quan Wright of the Cleveland Browns and Zxavian Harris of the New Orleans Saints are leaving their respective NFL teams to play for LSU . Both Wright and Harris played for Tigers head coach Lane Kiffin at Ole Miss.

Kiffin defended courting pro players on Monday during a press conference while being careful not to confirm any new signings, saying, "[They're] either going to play for you or they're going to play for someone else around the country."

On Monday, SEC presidents met virtually to support opposition to professional players coming back to play in college.

"College athletes, not former professional athletes, have been at the heart of the Southeastern Conference. Individuals who choose to leave college athletics, sign professional playing contracts, and compete professionally should not then be permitted to return to college competition," read part of the SEC's statement.

With Tuesday's decision, SEC schools are no longer allowed to have such athletes on their rosters for football or basketball. SEC commissioner Greg Sankey was granted "full and unlimited authority," which includes suspending a school from competition, according to Dellenger .

More discussions are expected Tuesday during a joint, two-day meeting of SEC presidents and athletic directors in Birmingham, Alabama — an unusual and significant gathering that was previously scheduled.

With the conferences all considering a ban, and the Big Ten's move to adopt such a policy, it could open them up to additional legal action and may put the leagues themselves at the center of new lawsuits — instead of the NCAA.

Additionally, if the conferences agree on a ban, they'd also need to determine the penalties for playing an ineligible player.

Whether the ACC and Big 12 follow the Big Ten's lead now remains to be seen.

articles.title: Caminhão quebra e trava trânsito na Avenida Centenário em Piracicaba | G1
articles.standfirst: Caso foi registrado no início da manhã desta quarta-feira (26) na Avenida Centenário. Nenhuma equipe da Semuttran monitorava o trecho até às 8h20.
articles.summary: Caminhão quebrado em Piracicaba trava a Avenida Centenário e motoristas improvisam sinalização com baldes diante da ausência de agentes de trânsito.
articles.body:
Um caminhão carregado com cinco toneladas de farinha de mandioca quebrou na Avenida Cententário, em frente ao campus da Universidade de São Paulo (Esalq-USP) em Piracicaba (SP) por volta das 7h desta quarta-feira (26). O veículo teve um problema mecânico. Há congestionamento no local.

Até às 8h desta quarta-feira (26), nenhuma equipe da Secretaria Municipal de Segurança Pública, Trânsito e Transportes (Semuttran) estava no local do incidente. Quem frequenta o trecho improvisou sinalização com pedaços de madeira e balde.

Às 8h15, ainda havia lentidão no trânsito no trecho, que costuma ter fluxo intenso de automóveis, principalmente nos horários de pico.

Caminhão carregado com farinha quebra, trava trânsito e avenida é sinalizada com balde e madeira em Piracicaba — Foto: Edijan Del Santo/EPTV

O caminhão está estacionado na esquina da Avenida Carlos Botelho. O motorista saía de Piracicaba e seguia sentido Campinas (SP).

O motorista afirmou que já acionou empresa responsável e aguarda chegada de mecânico para consertar caminhão e poder liberar a via.

Caminhão carregado com 5 tonelads de farinha quebra na Avenida Centenário em Piracicaba e via tem sinalização improvisada com balde e pedaços de madeira — Foto: Edijan Del Santo/Reprodução

Os motoristas que chegam em Piracicaba pela ponte do Shopping podem desviar pela Avenida Renato Vagner.

Essa é a segunda ocorrência de caminhão quebrado em via de Piracicaba. Na última segunda-feira (24), um outro caminhão carregado com 25 toneladas de sucata também teve uma pene mecânica e travou o trânsito na Rodovia Geraldo de Barros (SP-304).

articles.title: GWM anuncia o SUV híbrido Tank 400 para enfrentar o Toyota SW4 | G1
articles.standfirst: O jipão é o segundo modelo lançado da linha Tank, mas se destaca pelo motor mais potente, porte maior e foco no luxo, deixando as aptidões para o uso fora de estrada em segundo plano.
articles.summary: O jipão é o segundo modelo lançado da linha Tank, mas se destaca pelo motor mais potente, porte maior e foco no luxo, deixando as aptidões para o uso off-road em segundo plano.
articles.body:
A GWM anunciou o Tank 400, um jipão de sete lugares, maior que o Haval H9 e que chega ao mercado como híbrido plug-in para disputar a atenção de consumidores que já consideram o Toyota SW4.

À primeira vista, o Tank 400 não tem o mesmo visual totalmente quadrado do Haval H9 e do Tank 300 . Suas linhas são mais suaves e aproximam o modelo da proposta adotada pela Toyota em seu SUV grande.

O Tank 400 também traz alguns elementos que lembram o SW4, como a linha lateral que sobe ao chegar ao fim das portas traseiras e segue mais alta na janela logo atrás.

A grade frontal integrada aos faróis, posicionados mais acima, também lembra a do SW4. Nas dimensões, porém, o Tank 400 chega a ser 19 centímetros mais longo:

Comprimento: 4,98 metros (contra 4,79 metros do SW4);

Largura: 1,95 metro (contra 1,85 metro do SW4);

Altura: 1,9 metro (contra 1,83 metro do SW4);

Distância entre-eixos: 2,85 metros (contra 2,74 metros do SW4).

Para não dizer que o Tank 400 foi totalmente inspirado no SW4, o porta-malas abre para o lado e traz o estepe preso à tampa.

Por dentro, a comparação com o SUV que reina sozinho no segmento perde força, e o lado chinês aflora. Enquanto o SW4 é mais prático e menos requintado, o Tank 400 aposta em materiais mais macios ao toque, acabamento com cores menos contrastantes e uma lista de equipamentos mais ampla.

O destaque é a central multimídia posicionada acima do console central, com 16,3 polegadas, ao lado do painel digital de 12,3 polegadas. No SW4, o quadro de instrumentos ainda tem mostradores analógicos, e a central multimídia mede 9 polegadas. Abaixo do console, o Tank 400 traz dois carregadores de celular por indução

articles.title: VÍDEO: gata é resgatada após passar 3 dias presa dentro de cano no ES | G1
articles.standfirst: Para realizar o salvamento, agentes precisaram quebrar parte do concreto e cortar a tubulação com uma serra elétrica. Animal foi resgatado molhado e debilitado.
articles.summary: Para realizar o salvamento, agentes precisaram quebrar parte do concreto e cortar a tubulação com uma serra elétrica. Animal foi resgatado molhado e debilitado.
articles.body:
O resgate de uma gata que passou cerca de três dias presa em uma tubulação mobilizou uma equipe do Corpo de Bombeiros e da Defesa Civil em Muniz Freire, no Sul do Espírito Santo, nesta terça-feira (25).

O animal foi localizado em uma curva dentro do cano, em uma peça conhecida como “joelho” . Para realizar o salvamento, agentes precisaram quebrar parte do concreto e cortar a tubulação com uma serra elétrica (veja acima) .

Animal ficou preso em curva da tubulação

O caso teve início após a tutora acionar o Corpo de Bombeiros e relatar que a gata, que é chamada de Liz, havia desaparecido. Ela afirmou, ainda, ter ouvido miados vindos de um cano próximo a sua casa, na região do Jardim de Infância Monsenhor Aníbal Ademar Vieira da Cunha.

As equipes foram até o local e, durante as buscas, localizaram a origem dos sons. Foi constatado que o animal estava dentro de um trecho da tubulação e, após a abertura do cano, a gata foi retirada do local.

Gata estava presa dentro de uma tubulação em Muniz Freire, no Espírito Santo — Foto: Divulgação/Corpo de Bombeiros

“Foi uma ocorrência que exigiu muita atenção e persistência. Em alguns momentos, não conseguíamos mais ouvir os miados e não sabíamos exatamente onde a gata estava. Quando conseguimos identificar novamente o som, fizemos uma nova varredura e encontramos o ponto onde ela estava presa. Foi muito gratificante ver a gata sendo resgatada e retornando para casa”, contou o agente da Defesa Civil Marcos Vinícius.

Ao final do resgate, Liz foi entregue em segurança à tutora. O salvamento contou ainda com o apoio de uma moradora da região, que doou dois litros de leite para ajudar na recuperação do animal.

Gata Liz foi resgatada pelo Corpo de Bombeiros em Muniz Freire, no Espírito Santo — Foto: Divulgação/Corpo de Bombeiros

articles.title: Morador do DF que perdeu movimentos do corpo após acidente em praia dá primeiros passos e pode voltar para casa | G1
articles.standfirst: Felipe de Freitas foi atingido por uma onda e perdeu os movimentos dos braços e das pernas. Família diz que recuperação tem sido mais rápida que o esperado.
articles.summary: Felipe de Freitas foi atingido por uma onda e perdeu os movimentos dos braços e das pernas. Família diz que recuperação tem sido mais rápida que o esperado.
articles.body:
Felipe de Freitas – morador de Águas Claras, no Distrito Federal que perdeu os movimentos do corpo após ser atingido por uma onda em uma praia de Recife (PE) – já conseguiu dar os primeiros passos após o acidente , no último dia 10 ( veja vídeo acima ).

Ele também já foi liberado pelos médicos para voltar para Brasília , o que deve acontecer neste sábado (29), com o auxílio de todos equipamentos para garantir a segurança dele durante o voo.

A reabilitação começou no hospital em que Felipe ficou internado e continua em uma clínica de Recife . A fisioterapeuta Joseane Barbosa acompanha o tratamento desde o início.

"Ele não conseguia ficar sentado, se levantar da postura, mexer os braços de forma coordenada. Ele não conseguia mexer as mãos, flexionar os punhos, e tinha muita fraqueza nos quatro membros", lembra a profissional.

Felipe teve alta médica no dia 17 de agosto, uma semana após o acidente. A Paula, irmã dele, conta que a evolução tem sido mais rápida que o esperado .

"Lá no hospital, eu lembro que a fisioterapeuta fez os testes com ele, e ele não conseguia mexer praticamente nada do lado direito dele. Agora, o Filipe já consegue fazer movimento de pinça com todos os dedos da mão direita; a mão esquerda, ele já consegue movimentar sozinho, beber água sozinho", conta Paula Torres.

Morador do DF perde movimentos após acidente em praia de PE — Foto: arquivo pessoal

O acidente aconteceu no quarto dia de viagem da família. Quando tomava banho no mar, Felipe sofreu um grave acidente.

"Uma onda acertou a cervical do meu irmão e ele teve um traumatismo raquimedular cervical, em que ele perdeu todos os movimentos ainda dentro da água e quase morreu", diz Paula.

O Samu fez o resgate e os primeiros socorros de Felipe, que não tinha movimentação. No hospital, ele passou por uma cirurgia. Segundo o laudo médico, o trauma em Felipe comprometeu os movimentos dos braços e pernas.

Após tantos dias de incerteza, a família diz que consegue, enfim, respirar um pouco mais aliviada.

"Apesar do susto, apesar de tudo que a gente viveu, nós fomos abraçados e temos vivido passo a passo, dia a dia dessa recuperação do Filipe", completa a irmã Paula.

articles.title: São José: Aposta acerta 5 dos 6 números da Mega-Sena e ganha R$ 41 mil | G1
articles.standfirst: Prêmio principal acumulou em R$ 25 milhões e novo sorteio deve acontecer nesta quinta (27).
articles.summary: Prêmio principal acumulou em R$ 25 milhões e novo sorteio deve acontecer nesta quinta (27).
articles.body:
Apenas uma dezena separou uma aposta de São José dos Campos do prêmio milionário da Mega-Sena , sorteado na noite desta terça-feira (25).

Segundo a Caixa Econômica Federal, a aposta joseense juntou-se a outras 21 apostas que também acertaram a quina e cada uma delas faturou R$ 41.986,04.

Nenhum apostador faturou o prêmio principal, que agora acumulou em R$ 25 milhões. O novo sorteio é nesta quinta-feira (27).

Ainda de acordo com a Caixa, a aposta de São José foi registrada na Lotérica 9 de Julho, na Vila Adyana.

Veja os números sorteados nesta terça-feira (25):

Volantes da Mega-Sena — Foto: Rafa Neddermeyer / Agência Brasil

As apostas podem ser feitas em qualquer lotérica do país ou pela internet, no site da Caixa Econômica Federal – acessível por celular, computador ou outros dispositivos.

É necessário fazer um cadastro, ser maior de idade (18 anos ou mais) e preencher o número do cartão de crédito.

A probabilidade de vencer em cada concurso varia de acordo com o número de dezenas jogadas e do tipo de aposta realizada. Para a aposta simples, com apenas seis dezenas, que custa R$ 6, a probabilidade de ganhar o prêmio milionário é de 1 em 50.063.860, segundo a Caixa.

Já para uma aposta com 15 dezenas (limite máximo), com o preço de R$ 22.522,50, a probabilidade de acertar o prêmio é de 1 em 10.003, ainda segundo a Caixa.

articles.title: The Pakistan paradox: The rise of a pre-pardoned autocrat
articles.summary: International News: The geopolitical landscape of South Asia has shifted fundamentally following Pakistan's formal institutionalisation of an absolute military autocracy..
articles.body: The geopolitical landscape of South Asia has shifted fundamentally following Pakistan's formal institutionalisation of an absolute military autocracy. Through the passage of the 27th Constitutional Amendment and the subsequent enactment of the Defence Services of Pakistan Act 2026 on 20 August 2026, Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir has been granted unprecedented, legally enshrined absolute power. He now wields a degree of unchecked authority that surpasses any previous military dictator in the nation's history, presenting a grave escalation risk for regional stability and Indo-Pak relations.Pakistan has engineered a legal anomaly by the creation of a "pre-pardoned" ruler. The restructuring codifies a level of control that hollows out what remains of Pakistan's democratic and judicial institutions. The 27th Amendment grants Field Marshal Asim Munir sweeping, lifelong legal immunity that insulates him from any future criminal or constitutional prosecution, even after his tenure ends.By abolishing the Chairman Joint Chiefs of Staff Committee, the newly enacted Defence Services of Pakistan Act 2026 vests absolute operational command over the Army, Navy and Air Force directly in the office of the Chief of Defence Forces (CDF), held concurrently by Munir until at least 2030. The legislation grants the Field Marshal sole authority to "hire, fire, promote and retire" all personnel across all three branches of the armed forces. No head of state or civilian leader in a modern democratic framework commands such sweeping personnel and institutional leverage. Amendments to the National Command Authority (NCA) Act have further consolidated Pakistan's nuclear and strategic command frameworks directly under his immediate orbit.He will also play the role of the Prime Minister's principal military adviser on national security, defence and matters concerning the armed forces. The point to ponder is whether the Prime Minister will have the authority to go against his advice.The Contrast: Dictatorship Without AccountabilityThis absolute centralisation of authority marks a dangerous departure from historical precedent. During the 1999 peace process, General Pervez Musharraf unilaterally launched the Kargil infiltration. While he seized power in 1999 and remained President from 2001 to 2008, Musharraf still operated within a framework where he could later be tried, and ultimately sentenced, for high treason for suspension of the constitution in 2007, when he declared an emergency in a move intended to extend his tenure. Even though the charges remained pending and he was even allowed to leave the country, owing to the massive clout of the Army, there existed a provision to frame charges against him and pronounce a sentence. Under the 2026 legal framework, that internal accountability mechanism has been completely dismantled. Field Marshal Munir rules with total pre-facto immunity, leaving no domestic legal or political recourse to penalise strategic miscalculations or unilateral state actions.The explosive timingThis unprecedented consolidation of power comes at a time when Pakistan is facing severe institutional and socio-economic breakdown.The economy remains fragile, relying on external bailouts and suffering from structural inflation. Armed violence is surging across Balochistan and the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa border lands. Relations with the Taliban-led administration in Afghanistan remain volatile amid cross-border TTP terrorism. Underground political volatility persists, driven by the systemic suppression of Imran Khan and his widespread support base.Historically, when a Pakistani military regime faces an existential internal crisis, its default survival mechanism is to externalise domestic anger. A dictator holding absolute institutional control and total personal immunity is highly incentivised to trigger a controlled flashpoint with India to enforce national cohesion and divert public focus from a collapsing state.The threat matrix facing IndiaIndia must recalibrate its security doctrine to account for a nuclear-armed neighbour run by a commander answerable to no one.Future provocations may bypass deniable proxies or non-state actors entirely. Operations could be driven directly by state organs, secure in the knowledge that their commander-in-chief holds pre-pardoned immunity. Unchecked power over all military echelons allows the CDF to align regular forces with radical elements without institutional opposition.If a major cross-border terrorist attack is orchestrated under Rawalpindi's direct supervision, India's current military doctrine dictates a swift punitive response.Should India initiate a significant retaliatory counter-offensive, the conflict trajectory under a highly centralised, paranoid military command becomes entirely unpredictable. Pakistan's political class and its citizens must recognise that formalising absolute military supremacy through parliament is a short-sighted move that places the country on a precarious path. India must work out its options in light of this development in the neighbourhood.

articles.title: Colts' cornerback unit receives top 10 ranking entering 2026 season
articles.summary: In ESPN's most recent positional rankings, the Indianapolis Colts cornerback room, led by All-Pro Sauce Gardner, ranked No. 8 in the NFL.
articles.body:
When you think of the 2026 Indianapolis Colts , running back Jonathan Taylor is probably one of the first players that comes to mind. Another player that could come to mind is cornerback Sauce Gardner .

Although the All-Pro only played four games with the Colts last season after being traded from the New York Jets halfway through the year, he is one of the most talented players on Indianapolis' roster.

Gardner is probably a big reason why ESPN 's Mike Clay ranked the Colts cornerback room as a top 10 unit, coming in at No. 8 overall. There are only four teams in the AFC that are ahead of Indianapolis in the cornerback rankings, including their AFC South rival, the Houston Texans , who came in first.

Last season, the Colts gave up the second-most passing yards out of any team in the league, although they were top-10 in interceptions, as the cornerback room navigated injuries.

But when healthy, this could be one of the best starting units in football.

On the opposite side of Gardner is Charvarius Ward , who is going into his second season with Indianapolis. However, he only played seven games with the Colts last year due to injuries, although he was still quite impactful when on the field, allowing a completion rate of just 56% when targeted.

Ward's best season was back in 2024 when he was a Pro-Bowler and second-team All-Pro. That season, he recorded five interceptions and defended 23 total passes.

Overall, Indianapolis should live up to its top-10 ranking at cornerback as long as Gardner and Ward stay healthy.

articles.title: Bayer Leverkusen reject Aston Villa transfer approach for Cameroonian striker Christian Kofane
articles.summary: Aston Villa have had an approach rejected for Bayer Leverkusen striker Christian Kofane, according to The Athletic Leverkusen made it clear that they do not...
articles.body:
Aston Villa have had an approach rejected for Bayer Leverkusen striker Christian Kofane, according to The Athletic

Leverkusen made it clear that they do not intend to sell the 20-year-old.

Villa are long-time admirers of Kofane, who joined Leverkusen from Albacete last summer.

His first season in Germany yielded seven goals and nine assists in 44 appearances across all competitions.

His performances earned him a place in Cameroon's squad for the Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON), where they reached the quarter-final stage.

Villa are in the market for a potential replacement for Ollie Watkins , who is angling for a move to Saudi Pro League giants Al-Hilal.

They have rejected multiple bids, but Al-Hilal have an agreement with the player on personal terms.

Manager Unai Emery is unwilling to go through the season with Tammy Abraham and Brian Madjo as his options to lead the line.

Chelsea star Nicolas Jackson is also among their targets. He previously played under Emery at Villarreal .

They have had an approach turned down for Crystal Palace striker Jean-Philippe Mateta .

Villa should push the boat out for Jackson

Jackson is the most realistic choice for Villa. He has a respectable record of 24 goals and ten assists in 65 Premier League appearances.

The 25-year-old is familiar with the demands of Premier League football and understands how Emery works.

Kofane and Mateta would not be plug-and-play options for Emery, particularly as they would not have the luxury of pre-season training under him.

Jackson's selfless running and willingness to stretch defences make him the ideal fit for Villa.

With Villa set to compete on four fronts this season, they need a forward who can hit the ground running.

Jackson fits the bill and they must do whatever it takes to sign him before the transfer window closes.

articles.title: Youngsters 'not ready' says Watford boss Dionisi
articles.summary: Watford boss Alessio Dionisi made 11 changes only to watch his young side be dumped out of the Carabao Cup by Peterborough.
articles.body:
Watford boss Alessio Dionisi admits his young players are not yet ready for the first-team after their humbling defeat by League One side Peterborough United in the Carabao Cup.

The Posh ran riot in a 5-1 thrashing at Vicarage Road against a youthful Hornets side after Watford made a promising start to the league campaign under new head coach Dionisi, picking up four points in the first two games.

"I'm not happy, we're not happy but this is football. Yesterday, the young boys worked well [in training] but the official match is different," Dionisi told BBC Three Counties Radio.

"For them, it is difficult because [they] are not ready to stay in the first-team but, for me, it's not a problem. It is important for everyone to prepare for the next match against West Ham because it will be very, very difficult for us."

Dionisi made 11 changes from the side that started Saturday's Championship 1-1 draw at Wrexham , naming two 17-year-old's and eight players under the age of 20 as his side were comprehensively dumped out of the cup in the second round.

"I am sorry for our supporters but, for me, there wasn't another possibility for us to play every three days with the same line-up. It is impossible," said Dionisi.

"The result is terrible but, in this moment, we prefer to choose to prepare [for] the Championship [over the Carabao Cup].

"We need new players to complete this team. We need new players with experience but we will work with what we have."

articles.title: Washington Post fired Karen Attiah over social-media posts in 2025; an arbitrator has now ordered her reinstated with full back pay
articles.summary: US News: Karen Attiah, a former Washington Post opinion writer and the newspaper's founding global opinions editor, was fired on September 11, 2025, one day af.
articles.body: Karen Attiah, a former Washington Post opinion writer and the newspaper's founding global opinions editor, was fired on September 11, 2025, one day after conservative activist Charlie Kirk was shot and killed during a public appearance at Utah Valley University. The Post's termination letter accused Attiah of gross misconduct, saying her social-media comments about Kirk's death violated the newspaper's social-media policies, harmed the organisation's integrity and potentially endangered staff. Nearly a year later, independent arbitrator Sarah Miller Espinosa ruled that the Post did not have âgood and sufficient causeâ to terminate Attiah and had violated its collective bargaining agreement with the Washington-Baltimore News Guild. Espinosa ordered the newspaper to reinstate Attiah immediately, with full back pay and lost benefits. The decision is dated August 20, 2026, but was made public four days later, on August 24. The ruling brought a year-long dispute over newsroom discipline and expression to a close.What Karen Attiah posted after Charlie Kirk's killingAttiah made several posts on Bluesky following Kirk's death, discussing political violence and the public reaction to his killing. In one, she wrote that refusing to engage in what she called âperformative mourningâ for âa white man that espoused violenceâ was not itself violence. In another, she criticised what she described as the expectation that people show âcare, empty goodness and absolutionâ toward white men who espouse hatred and violence. Those posts were cited by the Post in the termination letter that ended her employment the following day. At the time, Attiah had spent 11 years at the newspaper, working as both an editor and opinion writer. She focused particularly on race, gender and international human rights and was the last Black full-time member of the Post's opinion desk when she was fired.Why the arbitrator found the Post did not have sufficient cause to fire herThe arbitration hearing took place June 4, 2026. In her ruling, Espinosa found that the Post had failed to establish that Attiah engaged in gross misconduct and had not shown âgood and sufficient causeâ to terminate her employment. The decision concluded that the firing violated the collective bargaining agreement between the newspaper and the Washington-Baltimore News Guild. Espinosa also rejected the Post's interpretation of Attiah's posts as racial or gender-based disparagement. The ruling said it was not reasonable to conclude that the posts referred to or disparaged all white men, or a particular white man, on the basis of race or gender. It also stated that recognising a person's race or gender does not by itself constitute disparagement on those grounds.The ruling noted that Attiah had worked at the Post for 11 years and had not previously been disciplined. Espinosa concluded that the newspaper had not met the standard required under the union agreement to justify termination without progressive discipline. She described the termination penalty as âabsolutely disproportionalâ and ordered the newspaper to reinstate Attiah immediately, with full back pay and lost benefits.What Attiah said after winning the arbitration caseAttiah publicly announced the ruling after the decision became public, saying that an independent arbitrator had ordered the Post to reinstate her with back pay. In a statement, she said the decision confirmed that she had been doing her job as an opinion writer and that doing that job was not misconduct. She added that she was ârelieved to finally have that record set straight.â The Washington-Baltimore News Guild and the Democracy Defenders Fund, which supported her case, welcomed the ruling as a significant victory for the union and press freedom. The Washington Post said it respects the arbitration process and declined to comment further on the ruling.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Max Verstappen theories over new F1 contract dismissed by Red Bull boss
articles.summary: Verstappen signed a contract extension until 2030 after being strongly linked with a move to Mercedes or McLaren
articles.body:
Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies quickly shut down two theories about Max Verstappen 's contract extension that were put forward by Nico Rosberg .

Four-time F1 world champion Verstappen signed a new contract with Red Bull until 2030 last week, which will extend the Dutch driver's partnership with the team to 15 years if he sees out his deal.

Rosberg, the world champion in Verstappen's debut Red Bull year in 2016, was in conversation with Mekies on the grid at the Dutch Grand Prix in Zandvoort when he put the 28-year-old's extension down to two reasons: a reported $80m-a-year deal and the culture Mekies has installed at the team since taking over from Christian Horner last year.

Yet in response, Mekies said: "So, both statements are not correct. It's down really to the trust that Max has in the 2,000 people we have in Milton Keynes [Red Bul HQ], chassis side, PU [power unit] side, and he knows what our people are capable of and he has chosen to put his trust in us for the future.

"So, we will try to pay him back for that. He's much more than just the fastest driver in the world for us and we'll try to make sure we give him a fast car as soon as possible."

Verstappen's future was shrouded in uncertainty given his dissatisfaction with this generation of car, alongside interest from Mercedes and McLaren, but the Dutchman has opted to remain with the only team he's ever known.

"It's phenomenal news, for the team of course, but also for us as a sport as a whole," Mekies added.

"It has been a great few weeks of discussions. From day one, Max said, 'I want to stay with you guys.' When we finally concluded everything, I said, 'Well, I thought you always wanted to stay anyway!'

"Jokes aside, we take the trust he is putting in us very, very seriously. It gives us a huge responsibility in terms of providing him with a package that he will need to fight for wins again.

"But there is nothing that we want more at Red Bull Racing than to come back to the top spot as soon as possible and we know that is also what Max wants."

Verstappen will be looking to bounce back following his massive first-lap crash at the Dutch Grand Prix at the next round in Monza (6 September).

articles.title: Man City complete the signing of Ayyoub Bouaddi
articles.summary: Manchester City have completed the signing of 18-year-old midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi for an initial €95 million (approx £81.3m).The Citizens have been looking...
articles.body:
Manchester City have completed the signing of 18-year-old midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi for an initial €95 million (approx £81.3m).

The Citizens have been looking to sign the highly-promising Moroccan from Lille all summer and have finally sealed the deal for the teenager, who has penned a five-year contract with the club.

Bouaddi becomes City's fourth signing this summer following the arrivals of Elliot Anderson , Jeremy Monga , and Gerónimo Rulli with the Manchester side looking much-changed under new manager Enzo Maresca .

"We discussed a lot of things and the future also because this is why I'm here – for the future," Bouaddi said on his arrival.

"We know that in the great club we need to win. We are going to see what's going to happen. What's important is that I'm going to give 100%, be always here for the team and then it's the future.

"I think here the most important [thing] is to win. In a big club you need to win and this is all that we are going to do. We are going to give 100% to achieve all of our goals."

Bouaddi came through the academy at Lille , making 95 appearances in total for the club.

articles.title: Franco Colapinto Pins Monza Hopes on Alpine’s Missing Upgrades: “Excited for the Future”
articles.summary: The 2026 Dutch Grand Prix proved to be a highly challenging weekend for Franco Colapinto, who crossed the finish line in 14th place while navigating treacher...
articles.body:
The 2026 Dutch Grand Prix proved to be a highly challenging weekend for Franco Colapinto , who crossed the finish line in 14th place while navigating treacherous, mixed conditions at Circuit Zandvoort. However, the Argentine driver's struggles were exacerbated by a significant mechanical discrepancy within the Alpine garage. While his teammate Pierre Gasly was equipped with the team's latest aerodynamic upgrade package and managed to salvage a championship point in 10th place, Colapinto was forced to battle the elements in older machinery.

Despite the obvious frustration of racing at a technical disadvantage, Colapinto told the media that he remains highly optimistic about his prospects for the upcoming Italian Grand Prix, where his car will finally receive the highly anticipated parts.

Colapinto on Making Moves Without the Upgrades

Zandvoort's sweeping, banked corners and unpredictable weather made it incredibly difficult for drivers to find a consistent rhythm. Despite lacking the ultimate pace of the updated Alpine, Colapinto still managed to execute several impressive overtakes during the wettest parts of the Grand Prix.

"It was difficult, but I think it was a good opportunity to make the moves, and I overtook four cars, so in those wet conditions, yeah, it was good to make some moves," Colapinto told the media.

However, the reality of the machinery deficit ultimately capped his progression through the midfield. He admitted that while the racecraft was satisfying, missing out on the points was a tough pill to swallow, particularly when seeing the success on the other side of the garage.

"But, of course, a bit annoying with the result, but at the end of the day, you know, we came without the upgrades, and it was tricky to score points," he explained. Noting Gasly's performance—Colapinto acknowledged the sheer value of the new parts. "Pierre was P10, so scored a point, which is positive, but for us, it was a bit tricky."

The Formula 1 paddock now heads straight to the high-speed "Temple of Speed" at Monza. As a pure power circuit requiring ultra-low downforce setups, aerodynamic efficiency is absolutely vital to remain competitive.

When asked about the upgrade situation and how frustrated he was to wait another week, Colapinto chose to focus entirely on the positives of the incoming development. Rather than dwelling on the Zandvoort disadvantage, the Alpine driver believes the new package will transform his race pace.

"Yeah, well, looking forward to the upgrades," Colapinto concluded. "I think they are a very big step, so excited for the future."

With Alpine fighting desperately for midfield supremacy in the Constructors' Championship, equipping both drivers with the full upgrade package could be the exact catalyst they need to consistently challenge for points across the European leg.

articles.title: Are you concerned by Man City 'fire sale'?
articles.summary: City boss Enzo Maresca made it quite clear during Friday's pre-match news conference that any player that is unhappy at the club is free to leave.  Maresca r...
articles.body:
Some of you have been sending questions in and Mathew asked me if Manchester City are having a "fire sale" and if the club are "tightening their belt for a specific reason".

City boss Enzo Maresca made it quite clear during Friday's pre-match news conference that any player that is unhappy at the club is free to leave.

Maresca revealed that Savio had said "from day one" that he wanted to move, while Omar Marmoush has been unhappy with the amount of gametime he has had since his move from Eintracht Frankfurt . He is too good a player to be playing second fiddle to Erling Haaland .

Are you concerned with the exits? Tell us

Tijjani Reijnders and Nico Gonzalez have both failed to nail down first-team places and the club stance has always been, if a bid comes in that matches the valuation of a player, they are free to go if they wish.

City bought Reijnders for £46.5m last summer and made a £6.5m profit on him, while they recouped most of what they paid for Gonzalez last January.

Elliot Anderson has already come in, a deal has been agreed for both Ayyoub Bouaddi and Allan Elias, while speculation around signing Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea has not gone away.

I'm expecting City and director of football Hugo Viana to do some deals before the end of the transfer window.

articles.title: 'A very special day' - Bouaddi completes City move
articles.summary: New Manchester City signing Ayyoub Bouaddi says it is a "dream" to join "the best club in the world".  The 18-year-old Morocco midfielder has moved from Lill...
articles.body:
New Manchester City signing Ayyoub Bouaddi says it is a "dream" to join "the best club in the world".

The 18-year-old Morocco midfielder has moved from Lille in a £85.6m deal and signed a five-year deal with City.

Enzo Maresca's side moved to sign Bouaddi after selling central midfielders Rodri to Barcelona in a £65m deal, Tijjani Reinders to Al-Qadsiah for £52m and agreeing to let Nico Gonzalez join Newcastle in a deal worth up to £52m.

"This is a very special day for me and my family," Bouaddi said on the move.

"Manchester City are, for me, the best club in the world. It's a dream to be here and be able to call myself a City player. I have spent most of my life working hard to become the best player I can be and reach the top of the game.

"I've watched City for many years, and I love their style of play. City always try and play quality football. And they have shown they are winners – this club feels like it's built to win.

"I have plenty of improving to do. I am only 18. This is undoubtedly the best place for me to do that.

"This club demands trophies and I will give everything to make sure we are challenging for every title."

Bouaddi impressed at this summer's World Cup - starting five of Morocco's six matches in their run to the quarter-finals - after becoming a key member of Lille's side in Ligue 1 .

City Director of Football Hugo Viana added: "Ayyoub's potential is extremely high - a player equipped with everything a top midfielder needs.

"At just 18, he already has outstanding football intelligence and that will only improve under the guidance of Enzo.

"We have watched him very, very closely and throughout that process we have become increasingly convinced he is a huge talent who will thrive at City."

articles.title: Lindsey Graham's sister wins Republican primary to contest Senate seat in November
articles.summary: The Trump-backed candidate, whose brother Lindsey Graham died in July, has never previously run for elected office.
articles.body:
Voters in South Carolina have chosen Darline Graham, the sister of late Senator Lindsey Graham, as the Republican candidate to contest his US Senate seat in November.

Graham's bid received strong backing from President Donald Trump, who travelled to the state to campaign for her. Graham's victory is being seen as evidence of Trump's continuing influence over the Republican Party.

Graham is currently serving in the Senate as a temporary replacement for her brother, who died suddenly in July. She had never previously run for elected office.

Republicans and Democrats also held primaries in several other states on Tuesday, as they narrowed down their field of candidates for the midterm elections.

Political experts expect that Graham will now go on to succeed in the November election. South Carolina has not elected a Democrat to the Senate for decades.

The midterms more generally will decide which party controls the US Congress - which in turn will have a bearing on the second half of Trump's presidency.

Graham was running against right-wing Republican Congressman Ralph Norman, who sought to portray his opponent as a puppet of Washington politicians.

Lindsey Graham's sister chosen as replacement after senator's death

Curbing Russia, helping Israel and fighting Iran - Lindsey Graham's political identity

The head-to-head was set up after the pair emerged as the top two from a wider field of candidates during an initial contest earlier this month.

Norman is a supporter of Trump and has voted in favour of many of his policies. But in 2024, he initially backed Trump's primary opponent Nikki Haley as his pick for Republican presidential candidate.

With counting almost complete, Graham had received 52.5% of the vote, according to the BBC's US partner CBS News.

In a post on X, she thanked her supporters and the president, and said she was "deeply honoured and humbled" by the result.

During her primary campaign, Graham acknowledged her lack of political experience, particularly after stumbling during a foreign-policy question during a recent debate.

Asked about the US stance towards Taiwan, Graham had said: "I'm not that informed on national security." She added: "National security is not my thing, not my area of expertise, but I do support the military."

Trump's influence over the party was also tested in Oklahoma, where Mike Mazzei, a former state lawmaker endorsed by the president, took on Gentner Drummond, the state's attorney general.

The winner is widely expected to become the next governor in the heavily Republican state.

South Carolina was not the only state that held an election on Tuesday to replace a deceased lawmaker.

In Georgia, voters in the Atlanta area were tasked with choosing a replacement for Democratic Congressman David Scott, who died in April.

Marcye Scott, the daughter of the late congressman, was among those seeking office. But projections in US media show she was beaten by opponent Everton Blair.

Blair will therefore serve out the remainder of the term, which ends in January. In November, two other candidates will run to take over his seat in the new year.

articles.title: Man City sign Lille's Bouaddi for 100 mn euros
articles.summary: Manchester City have signed teenage Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille in a five-year deal the French club said Wednesday was worth 100 million eur...
articles.body:
Manchester City have signed teenage Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille in a five-year deal the French club said Wednesday was worth 100 million euros (£86 million, $117 million).

City moved for Bouaddi after selling Spain's World Cup winning captain Rodri to Barcelona and Tijjani Reijnders to Al-Qadsiah, with Nico Gonzalez also poised to leave the Etihad.

The 18-year-old rising star was one of the stand-out players at the recent World Cup, helping Morocco reach the quarter-finals before they were beaten by France.

Bouaddi will join England's Elliot Anderson in City's revamped midfield.

"This is a very special day for me and my family," Bouaddi said in a statement on the City website.

"Manchester City are, for me, the best Club in the world.

"It's a dream to be here and be able to call myself a City player. I have spent most of my life working hard to become the best player I can be and reach the top of the game.

"I've watched City for many years, and I love their style of play.

"City always try and play quality football. And they have shown they are winners –- this Club feels like it's built to win."

Enzo Maresca made central midfield a key area for new signings after replacing Pep Guardiola as City manager at the end of last season.

City are also believed to retain an interest in Chelsea midfielder Enzo Fernandez , but the Blues set a recent deadline for bids for the £120 million-rated Argentine that passed without a deal being done.

City were thrashed 3-0 by Arsenal in the Community Shield, but they started their Premier League campaign with a 2-1 win at home to Bournemouth on Sunday.

articles.title: Man City complete £86m Bouaddi signing from Lille
articles.summary: Manchester City complete the signing of Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille in a £85.6m deal on a five-year contract.
articles.body:
Manchester City have signed Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille in a £85.6m deal.

The 18-year-old joins on a five-year contract, subject to international clearance, with City paying £81.4m upfront plus £4.2m in add-ons.

Enzo Maresca's side moved to sign Bouaddi after selling central midfielders Rodri to Barcelona in a £65m deal and Tijjani Reinders to Al-Qadsiah for £52m.

He impressed at this summer's World Cup - starting five of Morocco's six matches in their run to the quarter-finals - after becoming a key member of Lille's side in Ligue 1.

"This is a very special day for me and my family. Manchester City are, for me, the best club in the world. It's a dream to be here and be able to call myself a City player," said Bouaddi.

"I have spent most of my life working hard to become the best player I can be and reach the top of the game.

"I've watched City for many years, and I love their style of play. City always try and play quality football. And they have shown they are winners - this club feels like it's built to win."

Bouaddi made 96 appearances for Lille after making his debut in 2023, helping them finish third in Ligue 1 last season.

At the age of 16 he became the youngest footballer to ever play for the French side on his senior debut against Faroese club KI in the Europa League, before announcing himself on the world stage by playing a starring role in Lille's Champions League victory over Real Madrid in 2024.

Bouaddi will form part of a revamped midfield, with City already bringing in England midfielder Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest for £116m.

Bouaddi functions as a deep-lying conductor and would complement Anderson, who is comfortable as a box-to-box midfielder as well as the number six role he plays for England .

City are also set to make an offer for Chelsea 's Argentina midfielder Enzo Fernandez but it remains to be seen whether a deal can be struck with the 25-year-old valued at £120m.

Bouaddi's signing comes after Brazilian winger Savinho , now known as Savio, joined Tottenham in a £75m deal earlier this week.

Spurs have also agreed a loan deal to sign City's Egypt forward Omar Marmoush , while Spain midfielder Nico Gonzalez is set to leave Maresca's side to join Newcastle in a £52m deal.

articles.title: Lake Travis, Vandegrift top our Class 6A rankings as we preview Central Texas high school football
articles.summary: Our 2026 high school football previews and district predictions for Class 6A include our first top-five rankings of the season, led by Lake Travis.
articles.body:
The American-Statesman takes a look at Class 6A districts around Central Texas as the high school football season gets underway.

Fab Five: Central Texas' top 5 teams from Class 6A

1. Lake Travis (14-1 last year, DI state semifinalist): The Cavs graduated 18 starters, but there's never a lack of talent. DBs Luca Antoun and Jeremiah Strong and LB Owen Aird lead what should be one of the area's best defenses.

This video created with the assistance of AI.

2. Vandegrift (12-2, DII state semifinalist): New QB Gavin Koester paces an offense that should thrive running the ball, and the Vipers are deep with talent at all three levels on defense.

3. Westlake (7-4, DII area round): There are more question marks than in the past decade for the Chaps. But like Lake Travis, Westlake always has talent. Wylie Nichols is one of Central Texas' better defensive backs.

4. Dripping Springs (12-2, DII regional finalist): Chase Ames is the area's most prolific 6A QB and has a massive offensive line to protect him. The Tigers seem primed for another double-digit win season.

5. Hutto (9-3, DI area round): WR/DB Jaiden Fields is one of the area's top three players. If the Hippos get good play from a new quarterback, the sky's the limit for the offense.

Our other playoff teams: Hutto, Cedar Park and East View

Notes: Cedar Park, East View, Leander and Rouse all make the jump to 6A, with Vista Ridge the district's seventh team. This district is also in Region III, which offers a much tougher playoff route than Region IV. … While Vandegrift and Hutto seem to be a level above the rest of the district, the battle for the last two playoff spots should be fierce. … Keep an eye on whether or not Vista Ridge makes the playoffs. If it does, along with Vandegrift, Cedar Park and Hutto, that would push the Vipers into DII. … East View safety Jalani Culpepper is receiving Power Four interest. … Cedar Park's David Cooper is the district's only returning starting QB. He threw for 1,925 yards and 19 TDs in 2025. … Hutto (Casey Walraven), Rouse (Mark Hopkins) and Leander (Ahmad Zaidan) all have new coaches.

Our other playoff teams: Westlake, Round Rock and Cedar Ridge

Key game: Lake Travis vs. Westlake (Oct. 23)

Notes: Westlake and Lake Travis move into a district with the five Round Rock ISD schools. … Westlake's Jackson Cook and Lake Travis' Jackson Koeppel are arguably the two best offensive linemen in Central Texas, with Cook committed to Texas. … Round Rock has something neither Westlake nor Lake Travis do: an experienced starter at quarterback. Dov Stickler returns after throwing for 1,850 yards and 15 TDs during the Dragons' final eight games. He also has one of the area's top WRs in TCU commit Dylan Jaeger. … Stony Point has a new coach in Dustin Pleasant after longtime coach Craig Chessher retired . … Cedar Ridge is looking for its first playoff appearance since 2022 and first winning season since 2021. QB Dylan Snoga accounted for 1,736 yards and 17 TDs as a junior. … Jerry Gardner is McNeil's new coach. … Westlake would need either Lake Travis or Round Rock to miss the playoffs to be in DI in the postseason.

Our other playoff teams: Bowie, Johnson and Hays

Key game: Dripping Springs vs. Bowie (Oct. 16)

Notes: Realignment strangely didn't put Dripping Springs in a district with nearby Lake Travis and Westlake, instead grouping the Tigers with fellow Hays County schools Johnson and Hays, Austin ISD's three 6A schools (Austin High, Bowie and Akins) and Del Valle. Hays moves up from 5A DI and Johnson returns to an Austin-centric district after playing south the last two years. … Dripping Springs is the overwhelming favorite, but don't count out Bowie. The Bulldogs return eight defensive starters and have a powerhouse RB in Rhys Moreno. … Johnson is the district's wildcard. The Jaguars missed the playoffs a year ago but welcome back QB Jonah Montgomery and eight other starters. … Austin High LB Ethan Kahle is arguably the best player the Central Texas public isn't aware of. He tallied 121 tackles in 2025 and leads the Maroons' hopes to reach the postseason. … Keep an eye on Hays RB Eyan Stigall. Hawks coach Mark Torres is high on his talent, and Stigall ran for 537 yards and seven TDs as a sophomore. … A DII regional final between Dripping Springs and Westlake seems likely.

articles.title: Man City complete record £86m deal for Rodri replacement
articles.summary: The Morocco international shone for Lille last term and continued his impressive run of form at the World Cup, with the 18-year-old now a key piece in the Ci...
articles.body:
Manchester City have signed Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille for £85m in a record deal for a teenager in Premier League history.

Bouaddi has signed a five-year contract at the Etihad Stadium, becomes their second midfield signing of the summer after Elliot Anderson .

City's midfield revamp has now cost over £200m – with Anderson a club record purchase at £85m – with the potential of a third arrival there and interest in Enzo Fernandez of Chelsea .

Bouaddi excelled in the World Cup for Morocco as a teenager and City see him as a talent with the ability to get better still.

Director of football Enzo Maresca said: "Ayyoub's potential is extremely high - a player equipped with everything a top midfielder needs.

"At just 18, he already has outstanding football intelligence and that will only improve under the guidance of Enzo [Maresca, the manager].

"We have watched him very, very closely and throughout that process we have become increasingly convinced he is a huge talent who will thrive at City."

Bouaddi, who was the youngest player in Lille's history, will be charged with replacing Rodri and Bernardo Silva , who have joined Barcelona and Real Madrid respectively.

City could lose four midfielders this summer, with Tijjani Reijnders moving to Al Qadsiah for £51m and Newcastle agreeing a £52m fee for Nico Gonzalez.

Bouaddi, who will take the No 32 shirt at City, said: "I am really, really happy – really proud to be here at one of the greatest clubs in the world.

"This is a very special day for me and my family. Manchester City are, for me, the best Club in the world. It's a dream to be here and be able to call myself a City player. I have spent most of my life working hard to become the best player I can be and reach the top of the game.

"I've watched City for many years, and I love their style of play. City always try and play quality football. And they have shown they are winners – this Club feels like it's built to win.

"The squad is world-class and Enzo is a top manager. And I'm really looking forward to playing at the Etihad Stadium, in front of all the fans.

"I think it was the right time because I was good in Lille, I felt very good, but I felt it was the right moment to step over and coming to City."

articles.title: Form the key in Swansea striker battle
articles.summary: Vitor Matos says his forwards will be judged purely on form as Zan Vipotnik, Adam Idah and Ross Stewart compete for game-time at Swansea City this season.  V...
articles.body:
Vitor Matos says his forwards will be judged purely on form as Zan Vipotnik , Adam Idah and Ross Stewart compete for game-time at Swansea City this season.

Vipotnik was the top scorer in the Championship in 2025-26, but his sparkling form last term did not save the Slovenia international from being left out of Matos' starting side in last weekend's draw with Sheffield United.

Vipotnik had begun Swansea's opening-day victory over Stoke City, but was substituted after a low-key display as Idah came on to Swansea's winner at the Bet365 Stadium.

Republic of Ireland international Idah was picked against the Blades and produced an effective display before Vipotnik and new recruit Ross Stewart featured as substitute.

"It's about performance, nothing more," said Swansea head coach Matos.

"That doesn't change for striker, midfielder or winger.

"Who we use, when they are all in shape and on their best moment , it will depend on the opposition. When one is in a better moment than the other, then it's about us taking the best of that one and then we keep moving, like in all the positions."

Questions remain over whether Vipotnik will still be a Swansea player after the transfer window closes next Tuesday.

Regardless of the transfer situation, Idah may be favourite to start at Derby County on Saturday given the solid shift he put in last time out.

"I think Adam gave us the physicality we knew we needed on that position because of the man marking and because of the one-v-one on the last line," Matos said.

"We didn't really connect the way we wanted to find him in the best moment, but he offered a lot.

"I think he was quite important to push the team to the opposition half and that's what we gained with him."

articles.body: A look back at Dolly Parton’s life and accomplishments. Sen. Darline Graham wins the GOP primary runoff for her late brother’s Senate seat. And NASA’s new telescope could change our understanding of the universe. Here’s what to know today. Dolly Parton, country music icon, dies at 80 Dolly Parton, who rose from a loving but impoverished upbringing in the mountains of East Tennessee to become the “Queen of Country” music, a Hollywood star and a beloved American icon, has died at 80. articles.title: Prince Harry and Meghan land in UK days after announcing move
articles.summary: Prince Harry, Meghan, and their two children are believed to have flown into the country privately from California.
articles.body:
The Duke and Duchess of Sussex have arrived back in the UK, BBC News understands.

Prince Harry, Meghan and their children Archie and Lilibet are believed to have flown into the country privately from California, and landed in Birmingham shortly before midday.

A spokesman for the Duke and Duchess of Sussex said "this is not something we would comment on".

There did not appear to be a police presence as Harry and his family left the airport, a source told the BBC.

Last week, it was reported that the couple would be relocating to the UK in August. They will not return to official duties but will live in Britain as non-working royals.

It is thought the family will base themselves at a private property outside of London in the Cotswolds area.

Archie and Lilibet have been enrolled in school and the new term is due to start next week.

The Sussexes left the UK and stepped back from their royal duties in early 2020, before settling in California in March that year.

King Charles was told of the move earlier this month. The family visited the King at his Highgrove home in July this year, but it is understood the move was not discussed.

Before that visit, Prince Harry and Meghan had not been in the UK together since they attended the funeral of Queen Elizabeth II in 2022.

Charity? Acting? The Cotswolds? What will Harry and Meghan's UK life look like?

The Prince and Princess of Wales have also been informed of their plans.

The Sussexes' security in the UK has been the subject of debate since the news of their return broke.

Last year, Prince Harry lost a legal challenge over the levels of security he and his family are entitled to while in the country.

The duke had sought to overturn a decision that had downgraded his security after he stopped being a working royal and moved to the US.

It is unclear what provisions will be made for their security in the UK and who will pay for it.

After the announcement of the Sussexes' intended return, a Home Office spokesperson said decisions on the security of royals were taken by the Executive Committee for the Protection of Royalty and Public Figures (Ravec), and the UK government's protective security system was "rigorous and proportionate".

Prince Harry has previously said that worries about safety have prevented him from coming to the UK and bringing his wife and children.

Last month, the duke and six other public figures lost their High Court privacy case against the publisher of the Daily Mail and Mail.

They face paying up to £34.5m to Associated Newspapers in legal costs.

articles.title: CIA chief held talks with Russian intelligence services, Kremlin says
articles.summary: John Ratcliffe travelled to the Russian capital on Tuesday in a rare and unannounced visit.
articles.body:
The head of the US Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) met figures from Russia's intelligence services during his unannounced visit to Moscow on Tuesday, the Kremlin has confirmed.

John Ratcliffe travelled to the Russian capital on Tuesday but neither side has shed any light on what prompted the unconventional meeting or what was discussed.

It is rare for American senior intelligence leaders to travel to Russia, with the last comparable meeting taking place in the months leading up to the full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

Ratcliffe arrived in Moscow on board a military plane which left later the same day.

The Kremlin ruled out speculation the CIA head met Russian President Vladimir Putin.

"There were contacts with the intelligence services," Dmitry Peskov told reporters.

"There were no meetings with the president of Russia. That's all I can say on the subject. Naturally, President Putin is briefed immediately about everything," he added.

Peskov made the comments in response to a question at his daily press briefing from a reporter at the Russian newspaper Rossiyskaya Gazeta, who asked if Vladimir Putin was informed about the CIA chief meetings and "at what level" they were held.

Putin's spokesman was also asked by the BBC's Russia Editor Steve Rosenberg what was the topic of the CIA talks.

"I have nothing to add to what I've already said on the subject," Peskov replied.

It was too early to say what impact this meeting would have over repairing bilateral US-Russian relations, he said, telling reporters: "How much this will impact the overall process of recovering our bilateral relations from the profound crisis they're currently in, it is premature to say."

But contacts between intelligence agencies are "a positive phenomenon, a positive process," Peskov added, saying they often continue "even during the most difficult moments" in relations between the two countries.

Ahead of the trip, the US told Ukraine that a senior delegation would be travelling to Moscow and asked Kyiv to suspend strikes until they had left, a senior Ukrainian official told CBS.

There has been no official comment on Ratcliffe's visitfrom the CIA, White House or Pentagon.

Ratcliffe appears to be one of the highest-ranking US officials to visit Russia during President Donald Trump's second term.

The last time a CIA director visited Moscow was in November 2021, when William Burns warned Russia against sending troops into Ukraine. Weeks later, the Kremlin launched its full-scale war on Ukraine.

Since then, the US has had strained relations with Russia, which has been isolated on the world stage and faced international economic sanctions.

Trump met Russian President Vladimir Putin at a summit in Alaska last year but the meeting did not lead to a breakthrough. Subsequent US-led peace talks between Russia and Ukraine appear to have stalled.

John Foreman, who served as a British military attachÃ© to Moscow between 2019 and 2022, told Radio 4's PM programme: "The Americans don't normally send such a high ranking official to Moscow unannounced at short notice unless something is up."

articles.title: In 1967, Emily Frew Oliver sold her familyâs Wyoming dude ranch to Grand Teton National Park but kept a life estate; 39 years later she gave it up, ending her familyâs 79-year stewardship of the historic ranch
articles.summary: US News: The 4 Lazy F Ranch sits on the west bank of the Snake River in Wyoming, just north of the Grand Teton National Park headquarters in Moose. Below the T.
articles.body: The 4 Lazy F Ranch sits on the west bank of the Snake River in Wyoming, just north of the Grand Teton National Park headquarters in Moose. Below the Teton Range, the ranch preserves a part of the areaâs homestead and dude ranch history.The property was first known as the Sun Star Ranch. Bryant Mears filed a claim for a 160-acre homestead in 1914 after arriving in Jackson Hole as a dude at the Bar BC Ranch, according to History Jackson Hole. He later served in the US Army during the First World War before returning to the valley with his wife.Mears received his homestead patent in 1921, but he had already transferred the property to Edward Mears. Edward later sold it to William and Margaretta Frew in 1927. The family renamed it the 4 Lazy F Ranch, a name based on the 'four Frews'- William, Margaretta and their two daughters, Margaretta 'Peggy' and Emily.For the Frews, the property initially served as a summer retreat. They built the main lodge and sleeping cabins, along with other structures that helped shape the ranch. The layout followed a style associated with Rocky Mountain dude ranches, with the main lodge at the centre and sleeping cabins arranged around it.From family retreat to dude ranchThe Frew family made few additions to the property between 1927 and 1949. That changed after William Frew died in 1948 and Margaretta Frew died in 1949. Emily Frew Oliver inherited the ranch and decided to open it to paying guests in 1950.Emily and her husband, Henry Oliver Jr, ran the ranch together. Henry looked after outdoor activities, including pack and fishing trips, while Emily managed the cooking and cleaning staff. She also made sure meals were prepared for both guests and staff.The ranch offered a different type of stay from many dude ranches in the valley. While a typical dude ranch stay was around two weeks, the 4 Lazy F accepted visitors for anything from an overnight stay to several weeks. A Union Pacific Railroad guide from around 1960 advertised rooms with meals, riding, swimming, fishing and pack trips to Yellowstone National Park.The ranch continued to retain much of its earlier character even as it operated for guests. Its main lodge served as the living and dining area, with a large central living room and fireplace. Sleeping cabins surrounded the lodge and created a communal area for guests. Irrigation ditches built during the earlier ranching period remained on the property, although they are no longer used.Property largely unchangedThe Olivers also continued the ranchâs agricultural activities. They kept milk cows, work horses, saddle horses, hogs and chickens. The family cultivated and irrigated land for winter feed but made few other changes to the landscape.The propertyâs natural appearance was part of its character. The lawn outside the main lodge was one of the main areas that was altered. It was first irrigated and flooded to keep the grass green, before the Olivers later installed a sprinkler system.As the ranch developed, some new buildings were added. A sleeping cabin and casting pond were constructed in 1952. Another cabin was moved from the Circle H Ranch in 1954, while the River Cabin was moved to the property in 1961. In 1964, a new cabin was built and parts of the caretakerâs cabin were modified.The ranch remained closely tied to the Oliver family. After Henry Oliver Jr died in 1977, their oldest son, Harry, helped Emily maintain and run the property. From 1977 to 2005, he spent every May through October at the ranch, overseeing operations and general maintenance.The 1967 sale to National ParkIn 1967, Emily Frew Oliver sold the 4 Lazy F Ranch to the federal government. However, she reserved a life estate, allowing her to retain her rights to the property during her lifetime.The sale marked a major change in ownership, but it did not immediately end the familyâs connection with the ranch. The Olivers continued to use and maintain the property for decades. The ranch formally stopped accepting paying guests during the 1990s.Emily Oliver eventually decided to voluntarily terminate her life estate. In 2006, she gave up the remaining rights and turned over management of the 4 Lazy F Ranch to the National Park Service.Today, the 4 Lazy F Ranch is vacant while the National Park Service evaluates possible future uses for the property. Its historic buildings remain, including the lodge, sleeping cabins, caretakerâs cabin, barn and other outbuildings.Several landscape features also survive. The lawn and ornamental plantings can still be seen, while native vegetation remains around the lodge and caretakerâs house. The irrigation ditches are also still visible across the property.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
